title: Strict Koszul to quotient comparison on one K-flat resolution
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $t\in\Gamma(\mathcal C,R)$ with injective multiplication on $R$. Assume countable products of $R$-module sheaves are exact. Use unbounded derived categories with localization $\mathcal Q$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $j\geq1$ let $B_j=R/t^jR$ and $L_j=[R\xrightarrow{t^j}R]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$, augmented to $B_j$, with transitions $(t,1)$ and quotient reduction [def-pur-principal-koszul-quotient-towers]. Use right total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], restricted derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and the normalized Roos model $\mathsf R=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ in reordered coordinates $(v,u)$ with differential $(dv,-du-(1-s)v)$ [def-weil-strict-roos-model, lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison].

For every unbounded complex $M$ and every flat-term K-flat resolution $f:P\to M$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution], there is a span of strict tower maps
$$(M\otimes_RL_j)_j\xleftarrow{f\otimes1}(P\otimes_RL_j)_j\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_j}(\operatorname{Res}(P\otimes_RB_j))_j$$
whose arrows are levelwise quasi-isomorphisms. Its components induce canonical isomorphisms $\mathcal Q(M\otimes_RL_j)\cong\operatorname{Res}(\mathcal Q(M)\otimes_R^LB_j)$ in $D(R)$, compatible with all quotient transitions. The span gives an isomorphism
$$s_f:\mathcal Q\mathsf R_j(M\otimes_RL_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Q\mathsf R_j\operatorname{Res}(P\otimes_RB_j).$$
Let $u_M:M\to\mathsf R_j(M\otimes_RL_j)$ and $v_P:P\to\mathsf R_j\operatorname{Res}(P\otimes_RB_j)$ be the strict augmentations with components $m\mapsto m\otimes1$ and $p\mapsto p\otimes\overline1$, respectively, and zero shifted components. Writing $e=\mathcal Q(f)$, one has
$$s_f\,\mathcal Q(u_M)=\mathcal Q(v_P)e^{-1}.$$
For each $j$ the projection of this map is $\mathcal Q(p\mapsto p\otimes\overline1)e^{-1}$, the actual canonical quotient reduction. In particular these identities hold for a single $P$ simultaneously at all levels and identify the completion units themselves, without requiring $M$ to be K-flat or derived complete.

proof.text: Multiplication by $t^j$ is a composite of $j$ monomorphisms, hence is injective. Thus $H^{-1}(L_j)=0$, $H^0(L_j)=B_j$, and $\epsilon_j:L_j\to B_j[0]$ induces the identity on $H^0$; it is a quasi-isomorphism. Its square with the transitions commutes: in degree zero both composites are the quotient $R\to B_j$, and in degree $-1$ both are zero. The differential square for $(t,1)$ is $t^jt=t^{j+1}$.

source.place: Tags 06YN (definition-K-flat) and 06YU (definition-derived-tor), principal regular two-term resolution; elementary cohomology calculation

proof.text: Apply the bounded-above finite-free complex assertion of lem-sfb-ringed-finite-free-resolution-tensor with $B=R$, $K=L_j$, $b=0$, ranks one in degrees $-1,0$ and zero elsewhere, and the identity frames. It makes $L_j$ K-flat. Therefore lem-pur-kflat-tensor-quasiiso-independent, applied to $f:P\to M$ with second factor $L_j$, makes $b_j=f\otimes1_{L_j}$ a quasi-isomorphism for every $j$. This uses no K-flatness of $M$.

Apply lem-pur-kflat-tensor-quasiiso-independent to $\epsilon_j:L_j\to B_j[0]$ with second factor the given K-flat $P$. This proves $\epsilon_j\otimes1_P$ is a quasi-isomorphism. To put $P$ first, use the signed interchange $x\otimes p\mapsto(-1)^{rq}p\otimes x$ for $x\in L_j^r$, $p\in P^q$, and the same formula on $B_j[0]$. The total differential formula shows it is a chain isomorphism: the two coefficients become $(-1)^{(r+1)q}$ and $(-1)^{r(q+1)+r}$, respectively, equal to $(-1)^{rq+q}$ and $(-1)^{rq}$. Interchange is natural in degree-zero cochain maps. Conjugating gives precisely $a_j=1_P\otimes\epsilon_j:P\otimes L_j\to\operatorname{Res}(P\otimes B_j)$. Hence $a_j$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06YP (lemma-K-flat-quasi-isomorphism); signed total-tensor interchange, written out

proof.text: Put $X_j=M\otimes L_j$, $Z_j=P\otimes L_j$, and $Y_j=\operatorname{Res}(P\otimes B_j)$. Functoriality of tensor and the square in step 1 give strict tower maps $b:Z\to X$ and $a:Z\to Y$. In detail $b_j(1_P\otimes(t,1))=(1_M\otimes(t,1))b_{j+1}$ and $a_j(1_P\otimes(t,1))=(1_P\otimes\mathrm{red})a_{j+1}$. Localizing the component span gives $c_j=\mathcal Q(a_j)\mathcal Q(b_j)^{-1}:\mathcal QX_j\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal QY_j$. Apply lem-pe-kflat-scalar-tower-realization to $K=\mathcal Q M$, $e=\mathcal Q f$ and the rings $B_j$. Its computation comparisons $\epsilon_j^{\mathrm{der}}:\operatorname{Res}(K\otimes_R^LB_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal QY_j$ identify all strict reductions with the canonical derived transitions. Thus $(\epsilon_j^{\mathrm{der}})^{-1}c_j$ are the claimed component isomorphisms, compatible with every composite transition.

source.place: Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), K-flat computation; strict tensor naturality

proof.text: The Roos comparison lemma descends the strict cone construction to the derived category of towers, so it sends the levelwise quasi-isomorphisms $a,b$ to isomorphisms. Set $A=\mathcal Q\mathsf R(a)$, $B=\mathcal Q\mathsf R(b)$ and $s_f=AB^{-1}$. The stipulated coordinates are the braiding of the strict Roos model's coordinates: $(u,v)$ becomes $(v,u)$, and $(-du-(1-s)v,dv)$ becomes $(dv,-du-(1-s)v)$. Tower maps act diagonally in either ordering. This gives exactly the requested isomorphism on the specified normalized models.

Let $w_P:P\to\mathsf R Z$ have components $p\mapsto p\otimes1$ and zero shifted components. The tower transitions fix these components. They are cochain maps, since $d(1)=0$ in degree zero. In the Roos differential the extra term vanishes because $(1-s)(p\otimes1)_j=0$. Diagonal functoriality now gives strict equalities $\mathsf R(b)w_P=u_Mf$ and $\mathsf R(a)w_P=v_P$: in each unshifted coordinate the equalities are $f(p)\otimes1$ and $p\otimes\overline1$, and all shifted coordinates are zero. Localizing, $B\mathcal Q(w_P)=\mathcal Q(u_M)e$ and $A\mathcal Q(w_P)=\mathcal Q(v_P)$. Multiplication by inverses yields $s_f\mathcal Q(u_M)=\mathcal Q(v_P)e^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok); explicit augmentation calculation in the strict cone coordinates

proof.text: Projecting the last identity to level $j$ gives $\mathcal Q(p\mapsto p\otimes\overline1)e^{-1}$. Indeed evaluation in the strict Roos model selects the unshifted $j$th coordinate. By the unit identity $\epsilon_j^{\mathrm{der}}u_j(K)e=\mathcal Q(p\mapsto p\otimes\overline1)$ of lem-pe-kflat-scalar-tower-realization this is the actual derived quotient unit, under its specified comparison, rather than just some map to an isomorphic object. The Roos comparison identifies zero-shifted-component strict augmentations with the canonical derived-limit maps, so the identity also identifies the completion units. Every construction above used the originally given $P$ and $f$ for all $j$; no completeness or boundedness hypothesis entered.
